<conversation:message_for_turn> writes the committed message {direction, source_ids, target_ids, content, content_type, participants, provenance}, without the message's other members: inbound audio content is null, other content is kept as given, and absent content is null; the message's participants, at most 32 {ref, role} each with an optional boolean own and an optional resembles (at most 3 {ref, similarity}, similarity -1 to 1), are kept as given (absent or null is none), and others raise error.execution; a provenance's id, source, target and session_ref are taken when they are strings, else null, and its turn_ref is taken as given; without a session_ref an inbound message's is relationship-<its relationship context reference> and an outbound one's null.

<conversation:relationship_for_input> writes the index of the input's relationship: targetless input shares the first ambient relationship, other input the best scoring one in either direction (names equal, embeddings at least 0.85 alike, one to one); with none it appends a relationship whose context_ref is {"identity_groups":[...]} over the sorted identity groups, whose session_ref is relationship- and that, and whose participants are empty.

<conversation:participant_for_source> adds the source to the relationship's participants once, <conversation:fail_turn> drops it, and <conversation:detector_refs> writes [session_ref, participant] of every participant, ordered by session_ref and then identity.

<conversation:new_track_ref> writes a name as its own track, an embedding as track- and its unit vector's JSON, and null for no source; <conversation:content_for_detector> writes the stimulus that opens the source's turn: text/plain string content as a text stimulus, audio/* string content as an audio stimulus with its rate and channels, anything else as a content stimulus.

<conversation:complete_turn> writes the inbound message of the turns' product: their texts joined by spaces as text/plain when any has text, each distinct text once; else no content for audio/*; else the input's content; with the first turn's turn_ref, the given session_ref, and the given participants (none when absent).

<conversation:ingest_content> takes a stimulus into the open turn's content (a text's stripped text when not empty, an audio chunk with the first rate and channels, a content, an event as application/event; an image changes nothing), and <conversation:on_end> writes the closed turn {turn} with its text, audio or content, or {failure} at stage turn when it has neither text, audio nor content, or both text and audio.

<conversation:turn_participants> writes the participants a cognition handoff stamps for the turn: the input's string identities, source_ids as sources then target_ids as targets, each group in identity order, then the parent's data's participants, each once, at most 32; an embedding, an empty name, or a name over 200 characters is never stamped; an input without source_ids and target_ids, or carried participants that are not {ref, role}, raise error.execution and assign nothing.

<conversation:people_for_input> writes {input, people, voices, representatives} (decisions D194 and D205): each embedding of the input's source_ids, then target_ids, is the person memory holds whose representative voice (one compact i8: text per person) or whose voice heard earlier in the same input is at least 0.85 alike by cosine, unless another person comes within 0.05, else a new person person-<n> numbered on after the after number; input is the input with each embedding replaced by its person's ref and each list without repeats, people the refs created, voices [person_ref, embedding JSON text] for each embedding heard, and representatives [person_ref, voice] each new person's first voice in compact text; a voice row of another shape is skipped, and an after that is not a whole number raises error.execution and assigns nothing.
